description:
FILED s516b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-12) from the #1575 re-bless: with the board running each t-file from its dist root, JSON-PP's 16 `099_binaryNN.t` files find `./t/099_binary.pl` (they were `*FILE*` rows) -- and stop far short of perl.

REPRODUCE:  tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/JSON-PP-4.18-0 t/099_binary03.t   (~15 s; prints 1..1536 and NO row, exit 0)
perl:       cd ~/.cpan/build/JSON-PP-4.18-0 && perl -Ilib t/099_binary03.t        (1536/1536)

The driver (t/099_binary.pl): BEGIN sets JSONPP_FROM/TO from the chunk number, `plan tests => 32 * (TO - FROM + 1)`, then `for (FROM .. TO) { test join "", map chr(...), 0..$_; ... }` with `sub test($)` running eight encode/decode round trips through ok().  Measured (b2, s516b tree): chunk 00 runs 48 rows (rows 25 26 29 30 41 42 45 46 = ` - 0` ` - 1` ` - 4` ` - 5`, the ascii()-encoded round trips, FAIL for the `chr(rand(2**20) & ~0x800)` strings), chunk 01 and 02 run 8, chunks 03..15 run 0 -- and every run exits 0 without a message, i.e. the loop or the program ENDS silently (rule 12 says that is itself a bug).  Not the range: `for ($ENV{F} .. $ENV{T})` with the same BEGIN-set values counts 48 under PCL (probed, scratch/s516b/pr/rng.pl).  Next step: cut 099_binary.pl down to one chunk-03 iteration and print around each test() call.

Board rows: the three *PLAN* rows (00, 01, 02) + chunk 00's four failing descriptions + the thirteen *FILE* rows of 03..15 (still blessed under #1575 by their text; they are this task's now).

=== MEASURED (s523a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) -- TWO mechanisms + one runner gap; nothing swallows an exception ===
WHAT ENDS THE PROGRAM: t/099_binaryNN.t is `do "./t/099_binary.pl"`.  The do-file dies inside its first test() (JSON::PP's own decode_error: "invalid character 0x1 encountered while parsing JSON string" -- Fable's c3-json-099 probe, one chunk-03 iteration under ./runpcl), and `do FILE` CATCHES the die into $@ exactly as perl does (probe scratch/s523a/pr/doq/outer.pl: perl = PCL, "after do: [boom...]").  So there is no swallowed CL condition and no silent exit path in the runtime.  The program then ends through the TAP layer's END hook, which PRINTS "# Looks like you planned 1536 tests but ran 0." (perl would print "# No tests run!") and exits 0 (perl 255).
(a) THE CAUSE OF THE DIE = #3650 (filed): pack / unpack ignore perl's "a template that begins with U is in U0 character mode" -- unpack('U*', "\x83") answers UTF-8-decoded garbage, pack('U', 0x83) answers two bytes.  JSON::PP's _encode_ascii / _encode_latin1 (`unpack('U*', ...)`) and its \u decoder (`pack('U', hex)`) both go through it.  With _encode_ascii replaced by a `map ord, split //` copy the iteration runs to its END line (scratch/s523a/pr/c3patch.pl) but encoders 0/1/4/5 (the ascii ones) still fail on the decode half (pack 'U').  Chunk 00's four `- 0 / - 1 / - 4 / - 5` rows are the same: ascii mode on chars above 0xFFFF; `_encode_surrogates`' arithmetic and `sprintf "\\u%x"` were probed identical to perl (j1.pl).  The fix is in cl/pack-impl.pl, the USER-PARKED pack oracle -> NOT taken; Fable/USER decision (#3650 has the fix's shape).
(b) THE EXIT STATUS = #3651 (filed): PCL's Test::More never sets Test::Builder's exit status (failures -> F, short plan -> 255, "No tests run!") -- a design question because the sweep and the board key on the rc.
SHIPPED (rule 12, the visible half): tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows printed the stream + stderr only when a row FAILED, so a run that stopped short of its plan with zero failures showed nothing; it now shows them when ran < plan too.  Guard tools/t/run-dist-t.t row 7 (fails on 8038fac6).  099_binary03.t now shows "# Looks like you planned 1536 tests but ran 0." on stderr.
ACCEPTANCE NOT MET (blocked by #3650): 099_binary03 still 0 of 1536; no blessed row moved.  The 2 detector lines on the probe (decode_json parsed as a list operator, ($) installed at run time) are #3143's family, noted only.
subject: JSON-PP t/099_binaryNN.t from the dist root: the chunk runs 48 (00) / 8 (01, 02) / 0 (03..15) of its 1,536 rows and EXITS 0 with no error printed; chunk 00's ascii-encode rows `- 0` `- 1` `- 4` `- 5` fail for the chars above 0xFFFF
